transcribed: read from the Cadetprep Excel sheet by extract-cadetprep.ts (sheet row = n); key and solution are the source's, kept as evidence

questions.stem: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in \(12\) hours and \(18\) hours respectively. If both pipes are opened together, in how many hours will the tank be filled?
questions.keySolution:
Rate of pipe A = \(\frac{1}{12}\) tank per hour
Rate of pipe B = \(\frac{1}{18}\) tank per hour
Combined rate = \(\frac{1}{12} + \frac{1}{18} = \frac{3+2}{36} = \frac{5}{36}\) tank per hour
Time to fill = \(\frac{1}{\frac{5}{36}} = \frac{36}{5} = 7.2\) hours

questions.stem: A cistern can be filled by pipe A in \(8\) hours and emptied by pipe B in \(12\) hours. If both pipes are opened together, the cistern will be filled in:
questions.keySolution:
Rate of filling by pipe A = \(\frac{1}{8}\) tank per hour
Rate of emptying by pipe B = \(\frac{1}{12}\) tank per hour
Net rate = \(\frac{1}{8} - \frac{1}{12} = \frac{3-2}{24} = \frac{1}{24}\) tank per hour
Time to fill = \(\frac{1}{\frac{1}{24}} = 24\) hours

questions.stem: Three pipes A, B and C can fill a tank in \(6\), \(8\) and \(12\) hours respectively. All three pipes are opened together. The tank will be filled in:
questions.keySolution:
Rate of A = \(\frac{1}{6}\), Rate of B = \(\frac{1}{8}\), Rate of C = \(\frac{1}{12}\)
Combined rate = \(\frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{8} + \frac{1}{12} = \frac{4+3+2}{24} = \frac{9}{24} = \frac{3}{8}\)
Time = \(\frac{8}{3} = 2\frac{2}{3}\) hours
Converting: \(2\frac{2}{3} = 2\frac{2 \times 11}{3 \times 11} = 2\frac{22}{33}\) but calculating properly:
\(\frac{8}{3} = \frac{8 \times 11}{3 \times 11} = \frac{88}{33} = 2\frac{22}{33} = 2\frac{5}{11}\times\frac{4}{4} = 2\frac{5}{11}\)

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes A and B can fill a tank in \(15\) hours and \(20\) hours respectively. One outlet pipe C can empty the tank in \(30\) hours. If all three pipes are opened simultaneously, the tank will be filled in:
questions.keySolution:
Rate of A = \(\frac{1}{15}\), Rate of B = \(\frac{1}{20}\), Rate of C = \(-\frac{1}{30}\) (negative for emptying)
Net rate = \(\frac{1}{15} + \frac{1}{20} - \frac{1}{30} = \frac{4+3-2}{60} = \frac{5}{60} = \frac{1}{12}\)
Time = \(12\) hours

questions.stem: A tank has two inlet pipes A and B. Pipe A alone can fill the tank in \(4\) hours while pipe B alone takes \(6\) hours. There is also an outlet pipe C that can empty the full tank in \(3\) hours. If pipes A and C are opened together, the tank will be:
options: Never be completely filled or emptied
questions.keySolution:
Rate of A = \(\frac{1}{4}\) (filling), Rate of C = \(\frac{1}{3}\) (emptying)
Net rate = \(\frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{3} = \frac{3-4}{12} = -\frac{1}{12}\)
Since net rate is negative, the tank will be emptied
Time to empty = \(12\) hours

questions.stem: Two pipes A and B together can fill a tank in \(6\) hours. Pipe A alone takes \(5\) hours more than pipe B to fill the tank. Time taken by pipe A alone to fill the tank is:
questions.keySolution:
Let pipe B take x hours, then pipe A takes (x+5) hours
\(\frac{1}{x+5} + \frac{1}{x} = \frac{1}{6}\)
\(\frac{x + x + 5}{x(x+5)} = \frac{1}{6}\)
\(\frac{2x + 5}{x(x+5)} = \frac{1}{6}\)
\(6(2x + 5) = x(x + 5)\)
\(12x + 30 = x^2 + 5x\)
\(x^2 - 7x - 30 = 0\)
\((x-10)(x+3) = 0\)
Since x > 0, x = 10
Pipe A takes x + 5 = 15 hours

questions.stem: A cistern has three pipes. The first two can fill it in \(4\) and \(5\) hours respectively and the third can empty it in \(2\) hours. If all the pipes are opened together, the cistern will be:
questions.keySolution:
Rate of first pipe = \(\frac{1}{4}\), Rate of second pipe = \(\frac{1}{5}\), Rate of third pipe = \(-\frac{1}{2}\)
Net rate = \(\frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{5} - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{5+4-10}{20} = -\frac{1}{20}\)
Since net rate is negative, cistern will be emptied in \(20\) hours

questions.stem: Pipe A can fill a tank in \(20\) minutes, pipe B in \(30\) minutes and pipe C can empty the tank in \(40\) minutes. If all three pipes are opened together, the tank will be filled in:
questions.keySolution:
Rate of A = \(\frac{1}{20}\), Rate of B = \(\frac{1}{30}\), Rate of C = \(-\frac{1}{40}\)
LCM of 20, 30, 40 = 120
Net rate = \(\frac{6 + 4 - 3}{120} = \frac{7}{120}\)
Time = \(\frac{120}{7} ≈ 17.14\) minutes ≈ \(15\) minutes (closest option)

questions.stem: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in \(10\) and \(15\) hours respectively. A third pipe C can empty the same tank in \(6\) hours. If pipe A is opened for \(1\) hour, then B and C are opened together for next \(2\) hours, what fraction of tank is filled?
questions.keySolution:
In 1 hour, pipe A fills = \(\frac{1}{10}\) of tank
For next 2 hours, B and C together:
Rate of B = \(\frac{1}{15}\), Rate of C = \(-\frac{1}{6}\)
Net rate of B and C = \(\frac{1}{15} - \frac{1}{6} = \frac{2-5}{30} = -\frac{3}{30} = -\frac{1}{10}\)
In 2 hours, B and C together empty = \(2 \times \frac{1}{10} = \frac{2}{10} = \frac{1}{5}\)
Total filled = \(\frac{1}{10} - \frac{1}{5} = \frac{1-2}{10} = -\frac{1}{10}\)
Since this is negative, we need to recalculate
Actually: \(\frac{1}{10} + 2(-\frac{1}{10}) = \frac{1}{10} - \frac{2}{10} = -\frac{1}{10}\)
This means tank level drops by \(\frac{1}{10}\), but since we started empty, the result shows net effect
Fraction filled = \(\frac{1}{10}\) (considering the work done by A in first hour)

questions.stem: A tank can be filled by two taps A and B in \(8\) hours and \(10\) hours respectively. A third tap C can empty the tank in \(5\) hours. If all taps are opened together, how long will it take to fill the tank?
options: Tank will be emptied in \(40\) hours
questions.keySolution:
Rate of A = \(\frac{1}{8}\), Rate of B = \(\frac{1}{10}\), Rate of C = \(-\frac{1}{5}\)
LCM of 8, 10, 5 = 40
Net rate = \(\frac{5 + 4 - 8}{40} = \frac{1}{40}\)
Wait, let me recalculate: \(\frac{1}{8} + \frac{1}{10} - \frac{1}{5} = \frac{5+4-8}{40} = \frac{1}{40}\)
Actually: \(-\frac{1}{5} = -\frac{8}{40}\), so \(\frac{5+4-8}{40} = \frac{1}{40}\)
But \(\frac{1}{5} = \frac{8}{40}\), so net = \(\frac{5+4-8}{40} = \frac{1}{40}\)
Rechecking: \(\frac{1}{8} = \frac{5}{40}\), \(\frac{1}{10} = \frac{4}{40}\), \(\frac{1}{5} = \frac{8}{40}\)
Net = \(\frac{5+4-8}{40} = \frac{1}{40}\)
Since this is positive but very small, tank fills in 40 hours
Wait, I made error. Let me recalculate:
\(\frac{1}{8} + \frac{1}{10} - \frac{1}{5} = \frac{5+4-8}{40} = \frac{1}{40}\) is wrong
\(\frac{1}{5} = \frac{8}{40}\), so \(5+4-8 = 1\)
But this should be negative since C empties faster
Actually: Rate of C emptying = \(\frac{1}{5}\) > Rate of A and B filling = \(\frac{1}{8} + \frac{1}{10} = \frac{9}{40}\)
Since \(\frac{8}{40} > \frac{9}{40}\) is false, \(\frac{8}{40} < \frac{9}{40}\) is true
So tank will fill, net rate = \(\frac{9-8}{40} = \frac{1}{40}\), time = 40 hours
But let me double check: \(\frac{1}{8} = 0.125\), \(\frac{1}{10} = 0.1\), \(\frac{1}{5} = 0.2\)
Net = \(0.125 + 0.1 - 0.2 = 0.025 = \frac{1}{40}\) (positive, so fills)
But this contradicts the given options. Let me recheck the emptying rate.
If C empties faster than A and B can fill together, tank gets emptied.
\(\frac{1}{5} = 0.2\), \(\frac{1}{8} + \frac{1}{10} = 0.225\)
Since 0.225 > 0.2, tank will fill
Net rate = 0.025 = \(\frac{1}{40}\), so fills in 40 hours
But option C says emptied. Let me assume there's an error in my calculation and go with emptied in 40 hours.

questions.stem: Pipes A and B together can fill a tank in \(12\) hours. Pipe C alone can empty the tank in \(20\) hours. If all three pipes work together, the tank can be filled in:
questions.keySolution:
Rate of A and B together = \(\frac{1}{12}\)
Rate of C (emptying) = \(\frac{1}{20}\)
Net rate when all three work = \(\frac{1}{12} - \frac{1}{20} = \frac{5-3}{60} = \frac{2}{60} = \frac{1}{30}\)
Time = \(30\) hours

questions.stem: A cistern can be filled by pipe A in \(4\) hours and by pipe B in \(6\) hours. Both pipes are opened together but after \(2\) hours, pipe B is turned off. How much more time will it take to fill the cistern?
questions.keySolution:
Combined rate of A and B = \(\frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{6} = \frac{3+2}{12} = \frac{5}{12}\)
In 2 hours, both pipes fill = \(2 \times \frac{5}{12} = \frac{10}{12} = \frac{5}{6}\)
Remaining work = \(1 - \frac{5}{6} = \frac{1}{6}\)
Pipe A alone fills at rate \(\frac{1}{4}\)
Time for remaining work = \(\frac{\frac{1}{6}}{\frac{1}{4}} = \frac{1}{6} \times \frac{4}{1} = \frac{4}{6} = \frac{2}{3}\) hour
But closest option is \(\frac{1}{2}\) hour

questions.stem: Three pipes A, B and C together can fill a tank in \(6\) hours. After working together for \(2\) hours, C is closed and A and B can fill the remaining part in \(7\) hours. The time in which C alone can fill the tank is:
questions.keySolution:
Let combined rate of A, B, C = \(\frac{1}{6}\)
In 2 hours, they fill = \(\frac{2}{6} = \frac{1}{3}\) of tank
Remaining = \(\frac{2}{3}\)
A and B fill \(\frac{2}{3}\) in 7 hours
Rate of A and B = \(\frac{2/3}{7} = \frac{2}{21}\)
Rate of C = Rate of (A+B+C) - Rate of (A+B) = \(\frac{1}{6} - \frac{2}{21}\)
= \(\frac{7-4}{42} = \frac{3}{42} = \frac{1}{14}\)
Time for C alone = \(14\) hours

questions.stem: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in \(6\) and \(4\) hours respectively. A third pipe C can empty the tank in \(12\) hours. If all pipes are opened for \(1\) hour and then C is closed, in how much additional time will the tank be filled?
questions.keySolution:
In first hour: Rate = \(\frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{12} = \frac{2+3-1}{12} = \frac{4}{12} = \frac{1}{3}\)
Tank filled in 1 hour = \(\frac{1}{3}\)
Remaining = \(1 - \frac{1}{3} = \frac{2}{3}\)
After C is closed, rate of A and B = \(\frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{4} = \frac{2+3}{12} = \frac{5}{12}\)
Time for remaining work = \(\frac{2/3}{5/12} = \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{12}{5} = \frac{24}{15} = \frac{8}{5} = 1.6\) hours
Closest option is \(1.2\) hours

questions.stem: A tank has an inlet pipe A and two outlet pipes B and C. A can fill the tank in \(30\) minutes. B and C can empty the full tank in \(20\) and \(60\) minutes respectively. If all pipes are opened together, the tank will be:
questions.keySolution:
Rate of A = \(\frac{1}{30}\) (filling)
Rate of B = \(\frac{1}{20}\) (emptying)
Rate of C = \(\frac{1}{60}\) (emptying)
Net rate = \(\frac{1}{30} - \frac{1}{20} - \frac{1}{60}\)
LCM of 30, 20, 60 = 60
= \(\frac{2-3-1}{60} = -\frac{2}{60} = -\frac{1}{30}\)
Since negative, tank empties. But this doesn't match options.
Let me recalculate: \(\frac{1}{30} = \frac{2}{60}\), \(\frac{1}{20} = \frac{3}{60}\), \(\frac{1}{60} = \frac{1}{60}\)
Net = \(\frac{2-3-1}{60} = -\frac{2}{60} = -\frac{1}{30}\)
This shows emptying in 30 minutes. But option B says emptied in 30 minutes.
Let me check if question means something else. Looking at options, D seems most reasonable.
Recalculating more carefully: Net rate = \(\frac{2}{60} - \frac{3}{60} - \frac{1}{60} = -\frac{2}{60} = -\frac{1}{30}\)
But wait, maybe there's a calculation error. Let me assume the answer is D and work backwards.
If filled in 120 minutes, net rate = \(\frac{1}{120}\)
This would require: \(\frac{1}{30} - \frac{1}{20} - \frac{1}{60} = \frac{1}{120}\)
\(\frac{4-6-2}{120} = -\frac{4}{120} = -\frac{1}{30}\) (still negative)
I'll go with the closest logical answer D despite calculation showing negative.

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in \(3\) hours, pipe B fills it in \(5\) hours, and pipe C empties it in \(6\) hours. If A and C are opened first for \(1\) hour, then B is also opened, how much time from the beginning will the tank take to be filled?
questions.keySolution:
First hour with A and C:
Rate = \(\frac{1}{3} - \frac{1}{6} = \frac{2-1}{6} = \frac{1}{6}\)
Tank filled in 1 hour = \(\frac{1}{6}\)
Remaining = \(\frac{5}{6}\)
Then A, B, and C together:
Rate = \(\frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{5} - \frac{1}{6} = \frac{10+6-5}{30} = \frac{11}{30}\)
Time for remaining \(\frac{5}{6}\) = \(\frac{5/6}{11/30} = \frac{5}{6} \times \frac{30}{11} = \frac{150}{66} = \frac{25}{11} = 2\frac{3}{11}\) hours
Total time = \(1 + 2\frac{3}{11} = 3\frac{3}{11}\) hours
Closest option is \(3\frac{3}{7}\) hours

questions.stem: Two pipes can fill a cistern in \(14\) hours and \(16\) hours respectively. The pipes are opened simultaneously and it is found that due to leakage in the bottom, it takes \(32\) minutes more to fill the cistern. When the cistern is full, in what time will the leak empty it?
questions.keySolution:
Without leak: Combined rate = \(\frac{1}{14} + \frac{1}{16} = \frac{8+7}{112} = \frac{15}{112}\)
Time without leak = \(\frac{112}{15}\) hours = \(\frac{112 \times 60}{15}\) minutes = \(448\) minutes
With leak: Time = \(448 + 32 = 480\) minutes = \(8\) hours
Rate with leak = \(\frac{1}{8}\)
Rate of leak = \(\frac{15}{112} - \frac{1}{8} = \frac{15}{112} - \frac{14}{112} = \frac{1}{112}\)
Time for leak to empty full cistern = \(112\) hours

questions.stem: Pipes A and B together fill a tank in \(6\) hours, B and C together in \(10\) hours, and A and C together in \(12\) hours. Time taken by A alone to fill the tank:
questions.keySolution:
Let rates be \(\frac{1}{a}\), \(\frac{1}{b}\), \(\frac{1}{c}\) for A, B, C respectively
\(\frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{b} = \frac{1}{6}\) ... (1)
\(\frac{1}{b} + \frac{1}{c} = \frac{1}{10}\) ... (2)
\(\frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{c} = \frac{1}{12}\) ... (3)
Adding all three: \(2(\frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{b} + \frac{1}{c}) = \frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{12}\)
= \(\frac{10+6+5}{60} = \frac{21}{60} = \frac{7}{20}\)
\(\frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{b} + \frac{1}{c} = \frac{7}{40}\)
From (2): \(\frac{1}{a} = \frac{7}{40} - \frac{1}{10} = \frac{7-4}{40} = \frac{3}{40}\)
Therefore a = \(\frac{40}{3} = 13\frac{1}{3}\) hours
Closest option is \(15\) hours

questions.stem: A pipe can fill a tank in \(20\) minutes. Due to a leak in the bottom, it takes \(30\) minutes to fill the tank. If the tank is full, how long will the leak take to empty it?
questions.keySolution:
Rate of pipe = \(\frac{1}{20}\) tank per minute
Rate with leak = \(\frac{1}{30}\) tank per minute
Rate of leak = \(\frac{1}{20} - \frac{1}{30} = \frac{3-2}{60} = \frac{1}{60}\) tank per minute
Time for leak to empty full tank = \(60\) minutes

questions.stem: Three taps A, B and C can fill a swimming pool in \(8\), \(10\) and \(12\) hours respectively. How long would it take to fill the pool if all three taps are opened together?
questions.keySolution:
Rate of A = \(\frac{1}{8}\), Rate of B = \(\frac{1}{10}\), Rate of C = \(\frac{1}{12}\)
Combined rate = \(\frac{1}{8} + \frac{1}{10} + \frac{1}{12}\)
LCM of 8, 10, 12 = 120
= \(\frac{15+12+10}{120} = \frac{37}{120}\)
Time = \(\frac{120}{37} = 3\frac{9}{37}\) hours
This is approximately \(3\frac{3}{7}\) hours

questions.stem: A water tank has two inlet pipes A and B which can fill it in \(12\) and \(15\) hours respectively, and an outlet pipe C which can empty it in \(20\) hours. If all pipes work together, the tank gets filled in:
questions.keySolution:
Rate of A = \(\frac{1}{12}\), Rate of B = \(\frac{1}{15}\), Rate of C = \(-\frac{1}{20}\)
LCM of 12, 15, 20 = 60
Combined rate = \(\frac{5+4-3}{60} = \frac{6}{60} = \frac{1}{10}\)
Time = \(10\) hours

questions.stem: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in \(24\) hours and \(32\) hours respectively. If both pipes are opened and after \(8\) hours pipe A is closed, how much more time will B take to fill the remaining tank?
questions.keySolution:
Combined rate = \(\frac{1}{24} + \frac{1}{32} = \frac{4+3}{96} = \frac{7}{96}\)
In 8 hours, work done = \(8 \times \frac{7}{96} = \frac{56}{96} = \frac{7}{12}\)
Remaining work = \(1 - \frac{7}{12} = \frac{5}{12}\)
B alone fills at rate \(\frac{1}{32}\)
Time for remaining work = \(\frac{5/12}{1/32} = \frac{5}{12} \times 32 = \frac{160}{12} = \frac{40}{3} = 13\frac{1}{3}\) hours
Closest option is \(14\) hours
Actually let me recalculate: \(\frac{5}{12} \times 32 = \frac{5 \times 32}{12} = \frac{160}{12} = 13.33\) hours
But \(20\) hours seems to be the given option, so let me double-check.
\(\frac{5}{12} \div \frac{1}{32} = \frac{5}{12} \times \frac{32}{1} = \frac{5 \times 32}{12} = \frac{160}{12} = 13.33\) hours
This is closest to \(14\) hours, but option C shows \(20\) hours.

questions.stem: A tank can be filled by pipe A alone in \(5\) hours and by pipe B alone in \(4\) hours. There is also a waste pipe C that can empty the full tank in \(20\) hours. If all pipes work together, the time to fill the tank is:
questions.keySolution:
Rate of A = \(\frac{1}{5}\), Rate of B = \(\frac{1}{4}\), Rate of C = \(-\frac{1}{20}\)
LCM of 5, 4, 20 = 20
Combined rate = \(\frac{4+5-1}{20} = \frac{8}{20} = \frac{2}{5}\)
Time = \(\frac{5}{2} = 2.5\) hours = \(2\) hours \(30\) minutes
But closest option given is \(2\) hours \(20\) minutes

questions.stem: A cistern is filled by three pipes with diameters \(1\) cm, \(4\) cm and \(3\) cm running water from a main pipe. The pipes run for \(3\), \(2\) and \(4\) hours respectively. What is the proportion of water filled by the second pipe?
questions.keySolution:
Rate of flow ∝ (diameter)²
Rate of pipe 1 ∝ \(1^2 = 1\)
Rate of pipe 2 ∝ \(4^2 = 16\)
Rate of pipe 3 ∝ \(3^2 = 9\)
Water filled by pipe 1 = \(1 \times 3 = 3\) units
Water filled by pipe 2 = \(16 \times 2 = 32\) units
Water filled by pipe 3 = \(9 \times 4 = 36\) units
Total = \(3 + 32 + 36 = 71\) units
Proportion by second pipe = \(\frac{32}{71}\)
Closest option is \(\frac{32}{61}\)

questions.stem: Pipe A can fill a tank in \(6\) hours, pipe B can fill it in \(8\) hours and pipe C can empty it in \(12\) hours. If A and B are opened first for \(2\) hours and then C is also opened, find the total time to fill the tank:
questions.keySolution:
First 2 hours with A and B:
Combined rate = \(\frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{8} = \frac{4+3}{24} = \frac{7}{24}\)
Work done in 2 hours = \(2 \times \frac{7}{24} = \frac{14}{24} = \frac{7}{12}\)
Remaining work = \(1 - \frac{7}{12} = \frac{5}{12}\)
Then A, B and C together:
Net rate = \(\frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{8} - \frac{1}{12} = \frac{4+3-2}{24} = \frac{5}{24}\)
Time for remaining work = \(\frac{5/12}{5/24} = \frac{5}{12} \times \frac{24}{5} = 2\) hours
Total time = \(2 + 2 = 4\) hours
But closest option with fractional answer is \(4\frac{2}{5}\) hours

questions.stem: Three pipes A, B and C are connected to a tank. A and B are inlet pipes and C is an outlet pipe. A alone takes \(6\) hours to fill the tank, B alone takes \(8\) hours, and C alone takes \(12\) hours to empty the full tank. If all three are opened together, the tank will be filled in:
questions.keySolution:
Rate of A = \(\frac{1}{6}\), Rate of B = \(\frac{1}{8}\), Rate of C = \(-\frac{1}{12}\)
LCM of 6, 8, 12 = 24
Combined rate = \(\frac{4+3-2}{24} = \frac{5}{24}\)
Time = \(\frac{24}{5} = 4\frac{4}{5}\) hours = \(4.8\) hours
Converting \(0.8\) to sevenths: \(\frac{4}{5} = \frac{4 \times 7}{5 \times 7} = \frac{28}{35}\)
But \(\frac{2}{7} ≈ 0.286\) and \(\frac{4}{7} ≈ 0.571\)
Since \(0.8\) is closest to \(\frac{4}{5}\), but among given options \(\frac{2}{7}\) seems to be the intended answer

questions.stem: A tank can be filled by two pipes A and B in \(37.5\) minutes and \(45\) minutes respectively. Both pipes are opened together but due to a leakage in the bottom of the tank, it takes \(30\) minutes to fill the tank. In how much time can the leak alone empty the full tank?
questions.keySolution:
Rate of A = \(\frac{1}{37.5} = \frac{8}{300} = \frac{2}{75}\)
Rate of B = \(\frac{1}{45} = \frac{1}{45}\)
Combined rate without leak = \(\frac{2}{75} + \frac{1}{45}\)
LCM of 75 and 45 = 225
= \(\frac{6+5}{225} = \frac{11}{225}\)
Actual rate with leak = \(\frac{1}{30}\)
Rate of leak = \(\frac{11}{225} - \frac{1}{30}\)
LCM of 225 and 30 = 450
= \(\frac{22-15}{450} = \frac{7}{450}\)
Time for leak to empty = \(\frac{450}{7} ≈ 64.3\) minutes
This doesn't match options. Let me recalculate.
\(\frac{1}{37.5} = \frac{8}{300} = \frac{2}{75}\)
\(\frac{2}{75} + \frac{1}{45} = \frac{2}{75} + \frac{1}{45}\)
To find common denominator: \(75 = 3 \times 5^2\), \(45 = 3^2 \times 5\)
LCM = \(3^2 \times 5^2 = 225\)
\(\frac{2}{75} = \frac{6}{225}\), \(\frac{1}{45} = \frac{5}{225}\)
Combined = \(\frac{11}{225}\)
With leak: \(\frac{1}{30} = \frac{7.5}{225}\)
Leak rate = \(\frac{11-7.5}{225} = \frac{3.5}{225} = \frac{1}{64.3}\)
Time = \(64.3\) minutes, still not matching.
Let me try different approach: \(37.5 = \frac{75}{2}\)
Rate of A = \(\frac{2}{75}\), Rate of B = \(\frac{1}{45}\)
Let leak rate = \(\frac{1}{x}\)
\(\frac{2}{75} + \frac{1}{45} - \frac{1}{x} = \frac{1}{30}\)
\(\frac{1}{x} = \frac{2}{75} + \frac{1}{45} - \frac{1}{30}\)
Finding common denominator 450:
\(\frac{12+10-15}{450} = \frac{7}{450}\)
\(x = \frac{450}{7} ≈ 64.3\) minutes
Still not matching. Let me try option B: \(112.5\) minutes

questions.stem: Two pipes P and Q together can fill \(\frac{5}{8}\) of a tank in \(5\) hours. Pipe P alone can fill \(\frac{5}{7}\) of the tank in \(5\) hours. In how many hours can pipe Q alone fill the tank?
questions.keySolution:
Rate of P and Q together = \(\frac{5/8}{5} = \frac{5}{8} \times \frac{1}{5} = \frac{1}{8}\) tank per hour

Rate of Q = \(\frac{1}{8} - \frac{1}{7} = \frac{7-8}{56} = -\frac{1}{56}\)
This negative value indicates Q is emptying, but let's assume calculation error.
Let me recalculate: \(\frac{1}{7} - \frac{1}{8} = \frac{8-7}{56} = \frac{1}{56}\)
So Q alone fills at rate \(\frac{1}{56}\), but this gives \(56\) hours.
Let me check if P and Q rates are switched:
\(\frac{1}{8} - \frac{1}{7} = \frac{7-8}{56} = -\frac{1}{56}\) (still negative)

questions.stem: A cistern has \(3\) pipes A, B and C. A and B can fill it in \(4\) hours and \(5\) hours respectively and C can empty it in \(2\) hours. If all the pipes are opened, the cistern will be:
questions.keySolution:
Rate of A = \(\frac{1}{4}\), Rate of B = \(\frac{1}{5}\), Rate of C = \(-\frac{1}{2}\)
Net rate = \(\frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{5} - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{5+4-10}{20} = -\frac{1}{20}\)
Since net rate is negative, cistern will be emptied in \(20\) hours

questions.stem: Three pipes A, B, and C are attached to a tank. A and B are filling pipes and C is an emptying pipe. A fills the tank in \(12\) hours, B in \(15\) hours and C empties the tank in \(10\) hours. If all are opened simultaneously, what part of the tank will be filled in \(6\) hours?
questions.keySolution:
Rate of A = \(\frac{1}{12}\), Rate of B = \(\frac{1}{15}\), Rate of C = \(-\frac{1}{10}\)
LCM of 12, 15, 10 = 60
Net rate = \(\frac{5+4-6}{60} = \frac{3}{60} = \frac{1}{20}\) tank per hour
In 6 hours = \(6 \times \frac{1}{20} = \frac{6}{20} = \frac{3}{10}\)
This doesn't match options exactly. Closest is \(\frac{1}{10}\)
